levels.L1: A feedback controller measures, compares with the target and corrects, over and over.
levels.L2: Each pass of the loop turns the latest measurement into a new command, many times a second.
levels.L3: Without the measurement (open loop), a change in load or wind goes uncorrected.

title: Target minus actual

levels.L1: The gap between where it should be and where it is.
levels.L2: Error = target height minus measured height, in metres; positive when the drone is too low.
levels.L3: The controller sees only this gap, not the drone's weight or the wind.

misconceptions: "The controller knows the drone's weight." A basic PID doesn't; it only sees the gap.

title: Push harder the bigger the error

levels.L1: Push harder the bigger the gap.
levels.L2: The P term is Kp times the error, in newtons; Kp is in N/m.
levels.L3: A bigger Kp shrinks the gap but makes the drone shoot higher, and the motors' maximum thrust caps it.

misconceptions: "Bigger gains are always better." They trade a smaller gap for more bounce, and motors have a limit.

levels.L1: Rushing toward a goal and going past it.
levels.L2: Here, how far the drone rises past the height it ends up at, in metres.
levels.L3: Less overshoot usually means a slower approach; damping (D) is the trade.

title: Never quite arriving under load

levels.L1: With P alone, a drone held up against gravity settles a little below its target.
levels.L2: At rest Kp times the gap equals the weight, so the gap is the weight divided by Kp.
levels.L3: A heavier drone or a steady wind needs a bigger gap; only a term that remembers (I) can remove it.

misconceptions: "P only should reach the target eventually if you wait." With a constant pull like gravity, it never does.

title: Push against the speed of change

levels.L1: Ease off early when rushing toward the target.
levels.L2: The D term is minus Kd times the measured speed, in newtons; Kd is in N·s/m.
levels.L3: Too much D makes the drone sluggish, and on real drones it amplifies sensor noise, so real controllers filter it.

misconceptions: "D makes the drone go faster." It does the opposite: it resists fast changes.

title: Add up the error over time

levels.L1: Remember how long the gap has lasted, and keep adding thrust until it closes.
levels.L2: The I term is Ki times the running total of the error, in newtons; Ki is in N/(m·s). At rest it holds the weight.
levels.L3: Too much I overshoots and rings, and past a limit it never settles; anti-windup stops the total growing while the motors are at a limit.

misconceptions: "I is just a stronger P." P reacts to the gap now; I reacts to the gap's history.
